items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. ... Nora Dutre on trombone. ... And I was on the bass.

ctx.x: They fired Jimmy Polar. Oh yeah. I remember that. You see, I'll give you the lineup of the band we left fairly well with. We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums. Okay. Then, they want to turn this boy loose, give him a note. Didn't give him no notice. Just fired him.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We finally got Noah Dutrae and Johnny, you see, myself... We had Noah Dutrae, we had Jimmy Pilar, Johnny Dodge, Lil... organized our regular group.

ctx.x: Oh yeah? Garland's New Orleans Jazz Band. Uh-huh. Jazz band, yeah.

Then, uh, Johnny Dodds come in town. We got a hold of Johnny Dodds. Nora Dutre was in the neighborhood. He used to come into Chicago and he'd come sit in with us. So, uh, Boyd H. Williams opened up the, uh, the, opened up this club on 34th Street, uh, Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…
Was it hard to find a piano player at the time?
